sourceFile: Diocesan_Cycle_of_Prayer_July_-_September_2026_v.2_Final.pdf, downloaded from the “PDF version” link on https://episcopalspringfield.org/resources/prayer-calendar.
notes: The diocese's own prayer-calendar page (https://episcopalspringfield.org/resources/prayer-calendar) currently publishes only the third-quarter 2026 PDF ("Diocesan_Cycle_of_Prayer_July_-_September_2026_v.2_Final.pdf"), confirmed by fetching the live page directly on 2026-09-29 (no Q4/Oct-Dec link present in the page's HTML). This file therefore covers only July 1 - September 30, 2026 (92 daily entries); January-June and October-December 2026 are not covered and are not fabricated here. A future file update (or a new file, per this corpus's own per-year convention) will be needed once the diocese publishes its next quarter.

This source is a DAILY cycle (one entry per calendar day of the quarter, not the weekly-Sunday pattern most other files in this corpus use), and every day's text is split into two parallel, separately-labeled cycles printed one after another: an "ANGLICAN CYCLE" line (the worldwide Anglican Cycle of Prayer, reprinted verbatim day-by-day into Springfield's own document) and a "DIOCESAN CYCLE" line (Springfield's own local commemorations). Both are transcribed for all 92 days.

Every day's ANGLICAN CYCLE line is recorded as a `category` subject (never `diocese`/`province`, which this schema reserves for scope-'communion' files) since this is a scope-'diocese' file reprinting outside Anglican Communion content verbatim -- the same treatment episcopal-missouri-2026.json gives its own reprinted Anglican Communion line.

The DIOCESAN CYCLE line is a genuine mix of content, handled as follows: (1) a day naming one or more specific Springfield congregations gets a `parish` subject per congregation (name + place), with any immediately-associated clergy names/roles or anniversary/consecration/admission detail folded into that subject's own `note`, exactly as this corpus's existing convention already folds founding-year/clergy detail into `note` (see episcopal-missouri-2026.json, episcopal-nebraska-2026.json); (2) a mention of the diocese's companion Diocese of Tabora, Tanzania's own parish/mission is recorded as a `category` subject (not `parish`), matching how Missouri's file already treats its own companion Diocese of Puerto Rico's institutions as `category` rather than `parish`; (3) the large majority of days name no congregation at all -- only a clergy birthday, wedding anniversary, or ordination anniversary tied to a person and their town (not a congregation), or a short original written prayer/collect with no proper noun in it whatsoever -- and each such day is recorded as a single `category` subject holding that day's full diocesan-cycle text verbatim; (4) when a day's text combines a named congregation with other, unrelated content in the same sentence or paragraph (a companion-diocese mission, an unrelated clergy birthday, a historical/administrative note tied to no single parish), each element was separated into its own subject in the source's own order, with nothing dropped -- verified subject-by-subject against the source text for every one of the 23 days this applied to.

Two Sundays (August 9 and August 16, "Bishops Sunday") break the otherwise-consistent every-Sunday pattern of naming one current Springfield congregation plus its Tabora companion parish/mission: neither names a specific congregation at all (August 9 is a general prayer for "all priests and lay people in the Dioceses of Springfield and Tabora"; August 16 names only the two dioceses' bishops). Both are transcribed as a single `category` subject per this file's usual no-congregation rule, not forced into a `parish` shape.

The source itself prints the SAME two congregations under two different names on different dates, both preserved verbatim rather than normalized to one spelling: "St. Thomas', Salem" (July 5) vs. "St. Thomas' Episcopal Church, Salem" (September 15); "Church of the Redeemer, Cairo" (August 6 and September 20) vs. "Redeemer Episcopal Church, Cairo" (September 15).

Preserved verbatim typos/oddities, confirmed against the rendered PDF page images (not just the extracted text) rather than assumed to be extraction artifacts: "The Diocese of Saint Andrews, Dunkeld and DunblaneThe Scottish Episcopal Church" (July 7 Anglican Cycle line -- missing comma/space before "The Scottish"); "The Diocese of BeniProvince de L'Eglise Anglicane Du Congo" (September 3 Anglican Cycle line -- same missing comma/space pattern); "The Rev Canon Shawn Denney" (within the July 12 Cathedral Church of St. Paul entry's note -- missing period after "Rev").

`liturgicalNote` is transcribed exactly as the source prints it for each date, which includes federal holidays the source itself annotated in the very same position as its liturgical labels ("Independence Day", "Labor Day") alongside genuine liturgical observances (saints' days, Ember Days, Sundays after Pentecost); both are disclosed source labels per this schema's own rule and neither is treated as authoritative for this app's calendar engines.

The diocese's own site footer self-identifies in all capitals ("THE EPISCOPAL DIOCESE OF SPRINGFIELD"); this file's `diocese` field uses standard title case, matching this corpus's existing convention for how other dioceses' all-caps site branding is recorded.

Built by extracting the source PDF's text with pdftotext -layout, then confirming single-column layout (no multi-column interleaving risk) by rendering and visually checking all 10 of the source's pages against the extracted text -- not just a sample -- given this source's daily granularity made a misattribution between adjacent days or between the Anglican/Diocesan lines especially easy to miss.
